issuer: the Insurance Corporation of British Columbia (ICBC), for the Province of British Columbia
note: ICBC's fees page and graduated licensing page (read 2026-10-30, and again on 2026-11-03) are built from a script payload, so their text was read from the saved pages' payload (ca-bc-fees.txt and ca-bc-glp.txt, the cells of each page in order, beside the saved HTML; ICBC writes a dollar sign there as $$). The fees page gives a first 5-year novice licence and a 5-year renewal at $75 each, and an original BCID valid for five years at $35. The graduated licensing page: a learner's licence from the 16th birthday; a novice licence after at least 1 year of practice (9 months at 25 or older); a Class 5 licence with restrictions after at least 24 months on the novice licence (if under 25); a full Class 5 licence after 12 months on that. The earliest full licence is therefore at 20 (16, plus 1, 2 and 1 years; 19 1/2 with an approved course), a sum of the page's periods kept as the age. Until 2026-11-03 the file held 21: read on 2026-10-30, the graduated licensing page gave the learner's stage as at least 2 years of practice; read again on 2026-11-03, it gives at least 1 year, and the age was corrected to 20. No youngest age for the BCID was read.

sources.title: ICBC, Graduated licensing
sources.said: You can get your L on or after your 16th birthday. ... After at least 1 year of practice with a qualified supervisor (or 9 months if you are 25 or older), you can take your first road test. ... 24 months* of safe driving (if you are under 25) ... After 12 months of safe driving with no prohibitions or suspensions on your Class 5 licence with restrictions, you will have a full Class 5 licence.
